name: Magnetic Hair Toy
description: A little magnet, thousands of grainy iron filings, and three faces in need of a change. Comb a moustache, chase a pattern, or abandon good taste entirely.

assets.credit: Original Oddly Dapper portraits, toy illustration and filing treatment

compatibility: Canvas 2D, Pointer Events and ResizeObserver; no third-party runtime or external assets. The original static portrait remains available without JavaScript.

Desktop mouse / trackpad, captured touch dragging, and keyboard: arrows move the magnet, Space holds or lifts, P picks up a pinch, Escape releases focus. Ordinary HTML controls provide matching actions.
1,200–7,000 individually positioned short marks. Typed arrays hold positions, velocities, orientation and selection; rendering batches marks into three paths, never one DOM element per particle.
Active physics runs at fixed 120 Hz substeps with bounded catch-up. Idle frames stop; hidden tabs, offscreen previews and Lab pause freeze simulation and challenge time.
Reduced motion skips the shaking animation and snaps directly manipulated filings into place. Explicitly started timed challenges still work. The experience is silent.
notes: Oddly Dapper is an original mid-century-inspired toy with three printed portraits: Milo the daydreamer, Cleo the botanist, and Cosmo the cat. It includes no protected toy artwork or branding.

Pressing the glass collects real existing filings within a swept magnetic radius. Carried marks follow the magnet with damped attraction, directional transport and deterministic strand offsets; lifting leaves them exactly in place.

Clumping changes the spacing and orientation of small groups. Each filing remains a short rigid mark with its own position and angle. There are no liquid metaballs, premade hair overlays or automated placement onto a pattern.

Six original templates cover moustaches, brows, beards, a crown, antennae and a spiral. Pattern scoring measures both path coverage and the fraction of placed filings near the target. A full dark face does not earn a perfect match.

Pick up a pinch moves existing grains from the tray onto the magnet; it does not create new particles. Changing the printed face keeps the filings in place. Changing density preserves existing geometry and adds new grains to the tray.

Shake returns the complete field to a deterministic reservoir. PNG export omits the cursor and hints. Artwork JSON stores all filing positions, angles, portrait and controls; Lab presets store settings only.
reuse: Download the standalone source ZIP or run pnpm lab:export magnetic-hair-toy. It contains all code, original portraits, preview, license, documentation and a custom background example, with no CDN or build step.
Use createMagneticLayer(canvas, settings, hooks) from engine.js to add movable filings over your own canvas artwork. Supply a background painter and optional overlay, change, frame and tick hooks.
FilingsField in model.js is DOM-independent. Submit move/engage/release inputs, step the deterministic simulation, inspect typed arrays, or serialize and restore the particle field.

illustration.js contains the optional portraits and mark rendering. challenges.js contains optional pattern geometry, scoring and a paused-clock state machine. The Lab UI in index.js can be omitted entirely.

The engine exposes update, setRunning, setContinuous, move, engage, release, setLatched, loadPinch, shake, reset, getState, serialize, load, png and dispose. README.md documents coordinate conventions, lifecycle and resource limits.
